parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, bathroom/facility rule, custody-placement rule or documented police sweeps of gender-nonconforming people appear in the dossier, and the trans-specific violence axis is entirely undocumented — so this sits below the tier-1 universal-exposure profiles (0.35–0.45) and well below the documented-targeting profiles (0.25). What is documented is serious: a live criminal statute (3 months–2 years) reaching same-sex conduct, which a trans visitor with a partner falls inside; police who refuse to investigate crimes against LGBTQ+ people; official hostility; pervasive social framing of LGBTQ+ people as threats; no anti-discrimination protection and no working recourse. The missing domestic gender-recognition machinery is a resident gap, not a visitor exposure. Worst documented tier is state-tolerated hostility with no remedy, aggravated by the enforceable statute — but no evidence it is systematically applied to gender-nonconforming travellers.
